1  THIS LAND ACQUISITION APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 04.06.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 2025:KER:39104 L.A.A.No.360 of 2015  3  JUDGMENT 1.
The claimant is the appellant in this appeal.

An extent of O.40 Ares belonging to the claimant was acquired as per Section 4(1) Notification dated 19.09.2006 under Land Acquisition Act, 1894, for the construction of Water Supply Project by the Kerala Water Authority.
The Land Acquisition Officer awarded compensation fixing the land value at the rate of Rs.18,876/- per Are.
As per the original judgment dated 02.06.2007, the Reference Court granted compensation for the land acquired as well as improvements therein fixing the land value at Rs.75,000/- per cent.
The said judgment was challenged by the respondents before this Court in LAA No.163 of 2012.
The said LAA was allowed, setting aside the judgment and remanding the matter to the Reference Court with respect to the compensation for the land alone.
Thereafter, the claimant took out a 2025:KER:39104 commission and the Advocate Commissioner had filed Ext.X1 dated 30.08.2014.
The Advocate Commissioner was examined as AW2.
The Reference Court granted compensation fixing land value at the rate of Rs.40,000/- per cent.
This appeal is filed claiming enhancement of compensation.
2. I heard the learned counsel for the appellant Sri.D.Sajeev and the learned Senior Government Pleader Smt.Rekha C.Nair.
3. The learned counsel for the appellant contended that it is in evidence that the acquired property is situated in an area having tourism importance.
It is reported by the Advocate Commissioner that the acquired property is situated very near to Vembanoor Junction having much commercial importance.
It is situated half kilometer from Aruvikkara Dam.
Considering the commercial importance and potentiality of the land, the Advocate Commissioner has reported Rs.2,50,000/- per cent.
The 2025:KER:39104 Reference Court ought to have relied on Ext.X1 report and the evidence of the Advocate Commissioner as AW2 to fix the land value.
Considering the land value reported by the Advocate Commissioner, the fixation of land value at the rate of Rs.40,000/- per cent is much on the lower side.

4. On the other hand, the learned Senior Government Pleader Smt.Rekha C. Nair argued that the original award passed by the Reference Court was set aside solely on the ground that the evidence of the claimant as AW1 alone was available before the Court and no data is available before the Court.
After the remand also, the situation was not improved, since the claimant did not produce any document to prove the land value.
Even for proving the land value at the rate of Rs.40,000/- per cent, there is no evidence before the Court.

The commission which was taken much after the date of Sindhu K.G vs State Of Kerala on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185927764/
2 acquisition could not be relied on as the Commissioner could not assess the 2025:KER:39104 potentiality of the land as on the date of 4(1) Notification dated 19.09.2006.

entities.text: Sindhu K.G vs State Of Kerala
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the Commission report and evidence of AW2 are not reliable.
5. I have considered the rival contentions.
6. The basic document for fixing the land value relied on by the Land Acquisition Officer is Ext.R5 document marked before the Reference Court.
It is a document dated 09.09.2004.

The 4(1)
Notification dated is 19.09.2006.
An extent of 13.5 cents of land and the building therein were sold for a total amount of Rs.3,00,000/-.
It is stated that the value of the building is Rs.1,50,000/-.
Excluding the building value, the value for land will come to Rs.1,50,000/-.
The land value would come to Rs.11,100/- per cent.
It is in evidence that Ext.R5 property is situated interior and the acquired property is situated on the side of the road.
The time difference between Ext.R5 document and the 4(1) notification is about 2 years.
Even if these factors are considered, the 2025:KER:39104 compensation could not be fixed above Rs.40,000/- by the Reference Court.
As rightly pointed out by the learned Senior Government Pleader, the commission was taken only in the year 2014 whereas the acquisition was in the year 2006.

It is true that the Commissioner has reported the land value @
Rs.2.5 lakhs per cent, but the data on which the commissioner relied on for reporting the land value @ Rs.2,50,000/- is not stated by the Commissioner either in Ext.X1 Report or when he was examined as AW2.
There is nothing before this Court to hold that the land value fixed by the Reference Court is on the lower side.
7. I do not find any reason to interfere with the judgment passed by the Reference Court.
Accordingly, this Appeal is dismissed without costs.

Sd/-
M.A.ABDULHAKHIM JUDGE Scl/RA Sindhu K.G vs State Of Kerala on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185927764/
